tagline.text: A historic mountain in central Cebu where President Magsaysay's plane crashed in 1957

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Magsaysay, Balamban, central Cebu Island, in the hills along the Cebu City boundary

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day to 2 days and 1 night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person, transport, entrance fee and snacks; camping and guide extra)

children.text: Mount Manunggal is the third-highest peak on Cebu Island and the place where the plane carrying President Ramon Magsaysay crashed on March 17, 1957. From the campsite on the ridge, now a National Historical Landmark, you can see the memorial and engine remains and look out over the sea toward Bohol and the Camotes.

Mount Manunggal sits in Barangay Magsaysay, Balamban, in the west of Cebu Island. Most sources, including Wikipedia, give its summit as about 982 meters, but some hiking blogs say 1,003 meters, so the figures differ by source. Either way, it ranks as the third-highest peak on Cebu after Osmeña Peak and Lugsangan Peak. The mountain lies inside the Central Cebu Protected Landscape, which links the Mananga–Kotkot–Lusaran river system, Sudlon National Park and the Buhisan, Mananga and Lusaran watershed forests, so it stands in what is something like the island's water tank.

What makes this mountain known to travelers is its history. In the early hours of March 17, 1957, a Philippine Air Force C-47 transport named "Mt. Pinatubo" took off from Lahug airport bound for Manila and crashed on this mountain. Twenty-five people died, including President Ramon Magsaysay, and only one newspaper reporter, Nestor Mata, survived. Investigators told the Senate that April that a drive shaft in the right engine had snapped from metal fatigue. Since then the site has hosted a memorial climb every year, and on April 24, 2012 the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) declared the crash site a National Historical Landmark.

The hike itself is not especially hard. The traditional route climbs from Cantipla or Tagba-o in Tabunan on the Cebu City side, or from a river jump-off on the boundary between Cebu City and Balamban, and is said to take roughly 4–7 hours for first-timers and 2–3 hours for experienced hikers. If you instead take the vehicle road up from the Balamban side, one guide says it is about a 30-minute walk from the eco park to the summit, which makes it possible for families. Depending on the route you choose, this can be a full day of hiking or a short outing to a historic site with a view.

This guide is for travelers staying in Cebu City who want to visit Mount Manunggal in a day or overnight. Access routes and fees change over time and no official rate sheet is published, so the numbers below are limited to ranges confirmed by several sources. Before you go, check the latest situation with the Balamban municipal tourism office, a local guide or a Cebu mountaineering club. Crowds gather around March 17 for the memorial events, so if you want a quiet hike, avoid those dates.

On one side of the campsite stands a monument honoring President Magsaysay, along with the engine cylinder block of the crashed C-47 "Mt. Pinatubo." It is said to be the last remaining part of the plane. It is not a flashy sight, but it shows the meaning of this mountain better than anything else. Walk around quietly and photograph with respect.

The NHCP declared the crash site a National Historical Landmark on April 24, 2012. It is closer to a memorial than a tourist spot, so basic courtesy means keeping your voice down and leaving no trash. Every March 17 the city of Balamban holds a wreath-laying at the site.

The campsite is a wide, gently rolling grassy area ringed by second-growth trees from reforestation. A nearby spring is said to keep flowing even in severe drought and El Niño years. The municipality has built concrete toilets and simple shelters, and during the annual climb the site can hold about 500 people.

On a clear day you can see Mount Tabunan and the surrounding ranges, Bohol, the Camotes Islands, the Camotes Sea, and the rivers and roads below the campsite. Many guides say the view is best at sunrise and sunset. Reviews also mention that communication towers near the summit give strong mobile signal.

The Tagba-o route on the Cebu City side has almost no forest shade and passes upland vegetable farms growing onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, eggplant, cabbage and carrots. Even at its narrowest the path is wide enough for two people to pass and has no big obstacles, so it is easy walking, but the sun is strong and you need a hat and sunscreen.
If you drive up the Balamban-side road, guides say it is about
30 minutes
on foot from the eco park entrance to the summit. It is introduced as a route for families with children or older relatives, but road surface and opening hours can change, so confirm locally.

blocks.title: Viewing tower and cross above the campsite

children.text: Above the campsite are a concrete viewing tower, a memorial cross and a small chapel built in the 1980s, at the height of the communist insurgency. The chapel is said to have been built for the spiritual needs of local residents.

Around March 17 each year the "Ramon Magsaysay Death Anniversary Climb" is held and draws many historians and hiking clubs. It is a good time to see the event atmosphere, but the campsite gets crowded and toilets and water can run short.

items.title: Short day trip
items.subtitle: A stroll to the summit from the Balamban eco park

children.text: From your Cebu City hotel, head toward Ayala Center and take a V-hire van to Balamban. Tell the driver in advance that you want to get off at the Mount Manunggal junction.
From the junction, take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) or a vehicle about 2 km up the narrow road to the eco park entrance and pay the entrance fee.
Walk uphill toward the summit for about 30 minutes, looking at the memorial, the engine remains and the viewing tower.
Enjoy a snack with the view from the campsite and walk around the spring.
Come down, eat lunch in Balamban town or at a roadside eatery, and return to Cebu City.
One guide says it takes about
2–3 hours
by car from Cebu City to this entrance, so you need to leave early in the morning. Check local schedules for public transport in both directions.
Leave downtown Cebu City for Tabunan via Talamban. It helps to contact a local guide or a Cebu mountaineering club member in advance.
Start walking at Tabunan and follow the farm trails of the Tagba-o route uphill.
Rest and eat lunch under a mango tree or near a house with coconut trees.
Reach the campsite, pitch your tent, wash rice with spring water and prepare dinner.
Watch the sunrise view, look around the memorial once more, eat breakfast, and start down around 08:00.
An older guide's schedule was a morning start, a lunch break, arrival at the campsite at 3 p.m. and descent at 11:30 a.m. the next day. Actual times depend on trail conditions and weather.
There are many direct flights a day from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB), and the flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and timetables change by season, so check when you book.
The usual way is to take a taxi or Grab from the airport to Cebu City and go on to the mountain from there. There is no public transport from the airport straight to the mountain.

items.title: From Cebu City to the Balamban-side entrance

children.text: Follow the Transcentral Highway toward Balamban, pass West 35, and about
1.5 km
beyond it turn at the Mount Manunggal sign. About
2 km
along a narrow road brings you to the eco park. One guide says it takes about
2–3 hours
by car from Cebu City.

By public transport, one known method is to take a V-hire van from Ayala Center toward Balamban, get off at the Mount Manunggal junction and take a motorcycle to the entrance. In 2019 the V-hire cost about
and the motorcycle about
, so prices may be higher now.
Another guide directs travelers to get off at the village of Gaas, and says a road of about
4 km
runs from Gaas toward the mountain, only partly paved. Confirm locally before you go.

items.title: From Cebu City to the Tabunan-side entrance

children.text: The traditional route goes north from Cebu City via Talamban to the Cantipla or Tagba-o start in Tabunan. An older guide said you reach Tabunan about
1 hour 30 minutes
after leaving downtown.
I could not find data on public transport or fares for this route. Many people are said to use a taxi, Grab or a local guide's vehicle.
On the mountain you move on foot, and motorcycles go up only as far as the eco park entrance.
To return to Cebu City after descending, flag down a V-hire toward Balamban or Cebu City at the roadside, or use a pre-booked car.

The best time to hike is the drier months from December to May. In the rainy season slopes are slippery and rivers rise, which can make the river crossing at the jump-off hard. At high elevation it gets chilly before dawn, so bring a jacket if you plan to camp.

Around March 17 the site is at its busiest because of the Magsaysay memorial events, with a wreath-laying and a commemorative climb. It is meaningful for feeling the historic atmosphere, but a quiet hike is hard.

There is almost no traveler accommodation near Mount Manunggal. Most people stay around Ayala, IT Park or Colon in Cebu City and leave early in the morning, or spend a night at the campsite. The campsite is said to have tents or simple shelters, toilets and parking. Hotel names and rates change a lot by season, so check recent reviews on a booking site.

There are almost no restaurants on the mountain, so it is better to bring water, lunch and snacks. After the descent you can eat local food in Balamban town or at roadside eateries, and many people return to Cebu City for Cebuano food such as grilled meat and lechon.
Leave before sunrise or early in the morning, because it takes 2–3 hours to reach the entrance from Cebu City.
On the shadeless Tagba-o route, bring a hat, sunscreen and at least 2 liters of water.
The campsite is chilly at dawn, so bring a thin warm jacket.
Even on the short route the trail is slippery when wet, so wear shoes with sturdy soles.
On the long routes it is safer and easier to avoid getting lost if you go with a local guide or a Cebu mountaineering club member.
There is no official rate sheet for entrance and camping fees, so carry plenty of small change and get a receipt.
Near the memorial, do not make loud noise or scatter food, and carry your trash back out.
Reviews say mobile signal is good near the summit but it may be weak in the middle sections, so download your map app in advance.
Around the March 17 memorial events it is crowded, so go early or avoid the date.
Entrance fees, access roads and opening hours differ by source and there is no official standard. Be sure to check the latest situation with the Balamban city hall or a local guide before you go.
In the rainy season slopes are slippery and rivers rise, which can make the river-start route dangerous, so postpone your trip if the weather is bad.
The Tagba-o route has almost no shade, so heatstroke and sunburn are possible at midday.
The road to the eco park is narrow and only partly paved, so wear a helmet and ride safely on a motorcycle.
This is a memorial site, so avoid drone flying and noise, and use fire only in designated places when camping.
The information in this guide covers what several sources could confirm in 2026, and some figures date from 2019 or earlier.
The main city of Cebu lies to the east below the mountain, and after the hike you can visit the Santo Niño Basilica and Magellan's Cross in
Cebu City
A viewpoint in the hills north of Cebu City as well,
Tops Lookout
is a good place to end the day with the city night view.
A flower garden sits at high elevation, and
Sirao Flower Garden
is easy to combine with a Mount Manunggal trip.
The protected landscape that Mount Manunggal belongs to, it connects the Mananga and Lusaran watersheds with Sudlon National Park. Confirm any entrance information locally.
